messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into French, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE French line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
ainsi la bête sans repos me fit, qui venant à moi en opposition petit à petit me repoussait là où le soleil se tait.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition (from Step 1) | Target Word/Phrase | Back‑Translation (French → English) | Status | |-------------|--------------------------------------|--------------------|--------------------------------------|--------| | tal | demonstrative “such” introducing the beast | ainsi | “thus / so” | OK | | mi | 1st‑person pronoun, object of the verb | me | “me” | OK | | fece | causative past “made” | fit | “made / did” | OK | | la | definite article marking *bestia* | la | “the” (feminine) | OK | | bestia | “beast” lacking peace | bête | “beast” | OK | | sanza | preposition “without” | sans | “without” | OK | | pace | noun “repose, peace” | repos | “rest, repose” | OK | | che | relative pronoun introducing clause | qui | “that / who” | OK | | venendomi | gerund “coming on against me” (motion toward speaker) | venant | “coming” (participle) | OK | | ’ncontro | preposition “against, in opposition” | en opposition | “in opposition” | OK | | a (1st) | part of idiom “a poco a poco” marking incremental step | à | “by / to” (first of the pair) | OK | | poco (1st) | adverb “little” indicating small degree | petit | “little” | OK | | a (2nd) | second marker of the idiom | à | “by / to” (second of the pair) | OK | | poco (2nd) | second “little” of the idiom | petit | “little” (second occurrence) | OK | | mi (2nd) | 1st‑person pronoun, object of *ripigneva* | me | “me” | OK | | ripigneva | imperfect “was pushing back” | repoussait | “was pushing back” | OK | | là | adverb of place “thither” | là | “there / thither” | OK | | dove | relative adverb “where” | où | “where” | OK | | ’l | clitic definite article “the” (for *sol*) | le | “the” (masc.) | OK | | sol | noun “Sun” | soleil | “Sun” | OK | | tace | verb “is silent” | tait | “is silent” (se tait) | OK |

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only French script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final French text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- **Line 58** - Original: *ainsi la bête sans repos me fit,* - Issue: **WRONG** – “ainsi” does not convey the demonstrative “such”. - Corrected: *telle la bête sans repos me fit,*
- **Line 59** - Original: *qui venant à moi en opposition petit à petit* - Issue: **WRONG** – the phrase “à moi en opposition” mis‑expresses “venendomi ’ncontro”. - Corrected: *qui venant contre moi petit à petit*
- **Line 60** - Original: *me repoussait là où le soleil se tait.* - Issue: **none** - Corrected: *no change*
